title: Who Erased 300 Years of Tamil History? | The Kalabhras #shorts

lines.text: Who erased three hundred years of Tamil history?
After about the two hundreds, records of the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas grow thin.
In their place stand rulers called the Kalabhras. Where they came from, nobody can say for sure.
lines.caps: in their *place | the *Kalabhras | where from? | *nobody | knows for *sure.

lines.text: And most of what we know was written by their enemies.
lines.caps: most of it | written by | their *enemies.

lines.text: About two centuries after them, a Pandya copper plate grant, found at Velvikudi, calls the Kalabhra a Kali king, who drove out countless great kings.
lines.caps: two *centuries later | a Pandya | *copper plate | *Velvikudi | a *Kali king | drove out | *countless kings.

lines.text: Then, it says, the Pandya Kadungon took the land back, late in the five hundreds.
lines.caps: then | it *says | *Kadungon | took it *back | late *500s CE.

lines.text: So for a long time, historians called it a dark age.
Now the doubt. Some scholars think the Kalabhras may have backed Jain and Buddhist monks, and that Tamil writing may have kept growing in these years.
lines.caps: now the *doubt | some *scholars | *Jain | and *Buddhist | Tamil *writing | kept *growing?

lines.text: Wreckers of Tamil country, or kings written out by the winners? Tell me below. Then watch the start again, and ask who was holding the pen.
